summary: An interior news page of the Semi-Weekly Miner (Butte, Montana) for March 20, 1889, running six to seven columns of dense editorial and news text with significant advertising on the right-hand margin and column. The page covers a wide range of subjects: editorial commentary on Wisconsin politics and the anti-slavery movement, speculation on the copper syndicate, coverage of St. Patrick's Day celebrations in Butte, personal mentions, and a lengthy report on the fraudulent use of alum in baking powder. The right-hand columns are heavily occupied by display advertising for patent medicines, mining equipment, and consumer goods, giving the page a mixed editorial-commercial character typical of Western frontier weeklies of the period.
headlines: OBSERVANCE OF THE SAINT'S NATAL DAY IN BUTTE
THE FRAUDULENT USE OF ALUM AND LIME

clipping_placements.placement_note: top of column 5, beneath a column rule; given a multi-deck display headline but flanked left by the copper trust story and right by full-page advertising

juxtapositions: The St. Patrick's Day celebration coverage, with its account of Irish fraternal orders parading through Butte, sits immediately adjacent to a column of large display advertisements for Dr. Price's Cream Baking Powder and patent medicines, creating a jarring editorial-commercial border.

A lengthy editorial on the 'barbarities' of Wisconsin's treatment of working people and the legacy of anti-slavery sentiment occupies the leftmost columns, while the Irish AOH parade story one column over celebrates Irish-American community life in Butte — two faces of the immigrant experience on the same page.
